en.headline: Lawmakers press Northern Metropolis university town in LegCo debate
en.dek: On the second day of the joint debate, Andrew Yao called the university town the main course of the Northern Metropolis, while Ng Wing-ka urged infrastructure first.
body: Lawmakers spent Thursday's session of a three-day joint debate on Hong Kong's first five-year plan and the Policy Address on speeding up the Northern Metropolis, with the planned university town the main point of argument.

Business sector member Andrew Yao said construction of the Northern Metropolis was an essential part of the five-year plan, and that the university town was its priority. He likened the town to the main course of the area, saying a strong project would draw technology firms, talent, leading companies and investors, and support Hong Kong's aim of being an international innovation centre.

Yao said industry, teaching and research had to connect. He backed a positioning for the Hung Shui Kiu university town in applied higher education for smart manufacturing, with a mix of industries and producer services, and links to parks including the Hung Shui Kiu industrial park. He also said he hoped the government would put more capital into the Hong Kong Investment Corporation so it could invest more flexibly in hard technology, life and health sciences, and new energy.

Business and Professionals Alliance leader Ng Wing-ka said upgrading the university-town planning group, led by the Chief Secretary, into a higher-level construction and development committee was a change of approach, not only a change of name. He argued that planning should put infrastructure first, including transport, roads and public facilities, and should account for cross-boundary passenger flows.

New Territories North member Yiu Ming of the Democratic Alliance for the Betterment and Progress of Hong Kong said he welcomed a clear direction for university towns at San Tin, Hung Shui Kiu and Ta Kwu Ling. He said he hoped established local schools would open branches there, and that international schools would also move in.

zh.headline: 立法會辯北都 姚祖輝稱大學城如主菜
zh.dek: 五年規劃與施政報告合併辯論進入北部都會區一節，姚祖輝聚焦大學城，吳永嘉則倡基建先行。
body: 立法會周四繼續為期三日的五年規劃及施政報告合併辯論，當日進入「加快北部都會區建設」一節，大學城成為多位議員的焦點。
商界議員姚祖輝說，北部都會區建設是五年規劃不可或缺的部分，重點在於北都大學城。他形容大學城如北都的一道主菜，項目出色便能匯聚科創企業、人才、龍頭企業及投資者，支撐香港成為國際創科中心。
姚祖輝又說，產、學、研需要銜接。他支持洪水橋大學城以智能製造應用型專上教育為定位，發展多元產業及生產性服務業，並與洪水橋產業園等聯動。他並期望政府向港投公司增加注資，以便更靈活投資硬科技、生命及健康科技、新能源及綠色科技。
經民聯黨魁吳永嘉認為，把由政務司司長領導的大學城籌劃及建設組升格為更高層次的建設及發展委員會，不只是改名，而是提升思維。他建議北都秉持基建先行，優先完善交通網絡、道路及公共設施，並兼顧跨境人流配套。
新界北議員、民建聯姚銘說，樂見政府明確新田、洪水橋及打鼓嶺三個大學城的定位，期望本地傳統名校能在北都開辦分校，並吸引國際學校落戶。
